captions.instagram:
There, But Not Here.

Pictures of my mother exist, but they're scattered across Houston, kept by different family members, tucked away in closets where they'll stay. Not thrown away. Just never looked at.

Swipe through.

From Not Plain. Read it at the link in bio.

pinterest.title: There, But Not Here: a memoir essay about the photos families keep
pinterest.description: A memoir essay about family photographs, the ones we protect and the ones scattered and tucked away, and how grief lives inside them. Narrative nonfiction from Not Plain, a memoir newsletter by Sarah.

slides.text: My mother isn’t in any of them, but she occupies every single one.

slides.label: that big grin
slides.text: My dad is grinning that big grin, the one that came out when he was genuinely humored and happy.

slides.label: a cake
slides.text: He’s holding a cake with the words Happy Birthday written in my mother’s cursive…

slides.label: the lens
slides.text: A moment in time captured through the lens of my mother.
